chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The purchase of stolen goods and goods of betrayal is not valid when it is recognized as such.

key_terms.الْخِيَانَةِ: Betrayal / Treachery (often referring to goods taken from a trust or partner)

ai.seo_question: Is buying stolen goods valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the invalidity of purchasing goods known to be acquired through theft or betrayal, emphasizing the buyer's due diligence in verifying the provenance of items. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that knowledge of the defect (such as being stolen) voids the transaction's validity, protecting the rights of the original owner. It serves as a foundational text for commercial jurisprudence regarding 'khianah' (betrayal/misappropriation) in market transactions.
